commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to select a patient by index
commitResults.messageBody:
Caregivers need a way to pick one patient and see their full record,
but there is no command to select a patient from the list.

Let's add `view INDEX`, which follows the same index rules and
invalid-index message as `delete` so the two commands behave
consistently. For now it only reports which patient was selected;
showing the details comes in later changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match view success message to the UI mockup
commitResults.messageBody:

mockup in the user guide shows "Showing patient: [NAME]".

Let's use the mockup's wording so the app matches its screenshot,
and add a test that checks the exact message text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track the viewed patient in the model
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel needs to know which patient to show, and must stay
correct when that patient is edited or deleted by another command.

Let's store the viewed patient in the Model as an observable value
that the view command sets and the UI can listen to.

ModelManager updates it when the address book changes:
* setPatient swaps in the new copy, e.g. after care info is added
* deletePatient clears it when the viewed patient is deleted
* setAddressBook clears it when the patient is no longer present,
  e.g. after clear

The panel listens to the viewed patient in the model, so it updates

commitResults.messageTitle: Add backup command to save a copy of the data
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have no built-in way to keep a copy of their patient data before
risky changes, such as editing the data file by hand.

Let's add a backup command that saves all patient data to
data/backups/mediconnect-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json. The folder is created if
missing, a second backup in the same second gets a -1, -2 suffix instead
of overwriting, and a failed write reports the reason without touching
the data. The clock and folder can be passed in so tests can fix both.

Fixes #132

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover more backup cases in tests and docs
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommandTest did not check that a backup leaves the model and
viewed patient unchanged, that the file name follows the clock's time
zone, or that the default constructor uses the system clock and
data/backups. The overridden methods in BackupCommand also had no
header comments.

Let's add tests for these cases, give each test a single behaviour,
and add JavaDoc to execute, equals and toString. The UG now lists
backup among the commands that ignore extra parameters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain why a backup failed and tidy its path
commitResults.messageBody:
When the backup folder was read-only, the error only repeated the file
path, because Java's AccessDeniedException uses the path as its
message. A relative backup folder also produced paths such as
tp/../../var in the result. Users could not tell what went wrong or
where the file went.

Let's name the folder in the error and give a readable reason for
permission and other file system errors, and normalize the paths shown
to the user. The UG now warns against running backup after the data
file failed to load, since the next command replaces that file.

New tests cover a read-only folder, a relative folder, filtered lists,
special characters, non-English locales and every failure reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop trailing full stops from backup failure reasons
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows error reasons end with a full stop, such as "The directory name
is invalid.", so a failed backup showed "invalid.. Your data has not
been changed." Blank reasons were also shown as-is, leaving an empty
gap in the message.

Let's trim trailing full stops and spaces from the reason, and fall
back to the generic reason when nothing is left. The test for a folder
that cannot be created now checks the reason itself instead of looking
for "null" anywhere in the message, which failed whenever the temporary
folder's path contained "null".

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy backup command code and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
BackupCommand had an unused MESSAGE_USAGE, which the other commands
without parameters do not define, and its two-argument constructor had
no @param tags. Its timestamp formatter took the default locale when
the class loaded, so the test that changed the locale later could not
affect it and checked nothing.

Let's remove the unused constant, document the constructor and the
less obvious constants, and build the formatter with Locale.ROOT so
file names do not depend on language settings. File names were
already ASCII in every locale tried, so behaviour is unchanged. The
misleading locale test goes, and the test comments now share one style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn against typing exit after a failed data load
commitResults.messageBody:
The backup caution told users to "close MediConnect" before copying an
unreadable data file. Typing exit counts as a command, so MediConnect
saves its empty data over the file, which is exactly what the caution
is meant to prevent. Closing the window or using File > Exit does not
save patient data.

Let's say not to run any command, not even exit, and name the two safe
ways to close MediConnect.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test relative and default backup folders
commitResults.messageBody:
Two planted bugs went unnoticed by BackupCommandTest: dropping
normalize() from the error message, and changing the default folder,
as the test compared it with the constant itself. The UG and help text
promise data/backups, which restore will also rely on.

Let's test an error with a relative backup folder and check the
default folder against data/backups directly. The setup shared by the
relative folder tests moves into a helper.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop null data files from crashing MediConnect
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file holding only null, or a patient list with a null entry,
made MediConnect quit at startup with a NullPointerException instead
of starting with no patients as the UG says. JsonUtil.readJsonFile
passed Jackson's null result to Optional.of, and
JsonSerializableAddressBook.toModelType called toModelType() on the
null entry. A preferences file holding null had the same effect.

Let's report both cases as a DataLoadingException, which MainApp
already handles for other files that cannot be loaded.

Fixes #152

BackupCommandTest kept relativeToWorkingDir as a private helper, but
the restore tests need the same relative folder paths.

Let's move it into TestUtil so that both test classes share one copy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split saving a backup out of BackupCommand.execute
commitResults.messageBody:
Restore needs to back up the current data before replacing it, and
must report where that backup went. BackupCommand.execute only gave
the path inside its success message.

Let's move the saving step into saveBackup, which returns the path of
the new file. execute calls it, so backup behaves as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add restore command to load a backup file
commitResults.messageBody:
Users could save backups, but had no way to bring one back short of
replacing the data file by hand.

Let's add restore FILENAME, which loads a file from data/backups. It
checks the whole file first and backs up the current data before
replacing it, so nothing changes if either step fails. Missing,
unreadable and invalid files each get their own message. The file name
must not contain a folder, so it cannot point outside data/backups.

Fixes #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the assert that rechecks the backup name
commitResults.messageBody:
getBackupFilePath asserted that the chosen file does not exist, right
after a loop that only ends when it does not. The assert added nothing,
and it checked the file system, which another program can change at
any time, rather than a condition that only our code can break. Codecov
also counted it as a partially covered line.

Let's remove it. The suffix loop and its tests still make sure that no
backup is overwritten.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the separator for same-second backups
commitResults.messageBody:
getBackupFilePath joined the suffix of a second backup in the same
second with an inline "-", while every other part of the file name
is a named constant.

Let's name it SUFFIX_SEPARATOR, like the other parts of the name.

execute ended by counting patients, choosing between "patient" and
"patients" and normalizing a path, below the level of its other
steps. The automatic backup's variable was called preRestoreBackup,
while the DG calls it automaticBackupFile, and MESSAGE_NO_PERMISSION
did not say that it was about reading.

Let's move the result into createSuccessResult, rename the variable
and the constant to automaticBackupFile and MESSAGE_NO_READ_PERMISSION,
and give the failure reason in backUpCurrentData its own variable, as
the other commands do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the backup and restore test helpers as verbs
commitResults.messageBody:
Some test helpers were named as nouns, such as restoreCommand(),
expectedSuccessMessage(), addressBookOf() and relativeToWorkingDir(),
while method names should be verbs.

Let's rename them to createRestoreCommand(),
getExpectedSuccessMessage(), createAddressBook() and
toPathRelativeToWorkingDir().

The coding standard says class variables should never be public
unless the class only holds data. JUnit can inject a @TempDir into a
private field, so the field does not need to be public.

The coding standard says class variables should never be public
unless the class only holds data. JUnit can inject a @TempDir into a
private field, so the field does not need to be public.

parse implements Parser#parse. Google's Java style, which the coding
standard follows on topics it does not cover, marks every override
with @Override, so the compiler also checks that it still overrides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the expected help commands unmodifiable
commitResults.messageBody:
EXPECTED_COMMANDS is named as a constant but held a mutable
LinkedHashMap. The coding standard uses Google's definition of a
constant, whose contents must not change. An unmodifiable view keeps
both the name and the order of the commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name help and detail panel tests in three parts
commitResults.messageBody:
The coding standard names tests as
featureUnderTest_testScenario_expectedBehavior, and lets a name drop
the last part, or the last two, but not the middle one. Four help
tests named only the feature and the expected behavior.

The detail panel tests started with an event such as
viewedPatientSet instead of the feature under test, so they now start
with viewedPatient and give the event as the scenario.

standard follows on topics it does not cover, marks every override
with @Override, so the compiler also checks that it still overrides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add NRIC and DOB field validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Patient stores NRIC and DOB as plain strings, so add accepts any
value for them, such as "S123" or "2021-02-30".

The MVP spec requires NRIC to follow the NRIC/FIN format and DOB to
be a valid date that is not in the future, to catch entry errors that
could lead to identifying the wrong patient.

Let's,
* add Nric and Dob field classes, following the existing Phone class
* store NRIC in uppercase so duplicate checks need no case handling
* store DOB as a LocalDate, which already rejects impossible dates
* parse both in add, and validate both when loading saved data
* document both formats in the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Update name, phone and address validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Name, Phone and Address use the AB3 rules and messages. Names allow
digits, phones only need 3 digits, and the messages differ from the
spec.

The MVP spec restricts names to letters, spaces, "/" and ".", and
phones to 8 digits with an optional +65, to catch entry errors early.

Let's,
* update the Name and Phone rules and all three messages to the spec
* reduce multiple spaces between words in names to one
* store phones without +65 so the same number is always shown the same
* update test fixtures with phones that are not 8 digits
* document the name and phone formats in the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow apostrophes and hyphens in names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names can only contain letters, spaces, "/" and ".". Real names such
as O'Brien and Mary-Jane are rejected, which testers are likely to
report as bugs. Names can also start with "/" or ".", e.g. "/Alex".

A name should allow common punctuation in real names, but still start
with a letter so that obvious entry errors are caught.

Let's,
* allow apostrophes and hyphens in names
* require names to start with a letter
* update the error message and the User Guide to describe the rule

The data file is saved as data/addressbook.json, a name left over from
AB3. The User Guide's data sections still refer to that file and to
"AddressBook", and do not say where the data is saved.

Users looking for their data should find a file named after the app.

Let's,
* change the default data file to data/mediconnect.json
* update the data sections of the User Guide to match
* add a FAQ entry on where the data is saved

commitResults.messageTitle: Update missing data file test for launch save
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual test for a missing data file says the file is created after
the first command. The app now saves the sample data to a new data
file on launch.

Let's update the expected result to say the file is created on launch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test data file creation when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
The catch block that handles a failed save of the new data file is
not run by any test, so Codecov reports the change as uncovered.

Let's add a test that makes saving fail and checks that the app still
starts with the sample patients.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention no spaces in phone error message
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone numbers written with a space, such as 9123 4567 or
+65 91234567, are rejected, but the error message does not say why.

Let's say in the message that the number should have no spaces.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test names starting with a slash or period
commitResults.messageBody:
Names such as /Alex and .Alex were valid before and are now rejected,
but no test checks this, so a later change to the rule could allow
them again without any test failing.

Let's add both as invalid names in NameTest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention unknown prefixes under field format table
commitResults.messageBody:
The table says an address can take any value, but once unknown
prefixes are rejected in the add command, a word such as x/12 is not
allowed in any field.

Let's add a note under the table that words like x/12 are not allowed
and point to the add command for details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention no spaces in phone format
commitResults.messageBody:
The phone error message now says the number should have no spaces,
but the Phone row in the field format table does not.

Let's add "with no spaces" to the Phone row so that the table matches
the message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show allowed first letters in NRIC message
commitResults.messageBody:
The NRIC error message says an NRIC is 1 letter, 7 digits and 1
letter, but only S, T, F, G and M are accepted as the first letter.
An input such as A1111111B already has that format, so the message
does not tell the user what is wrong.

Let's list the allowed first letters in the message, using the same
wording as the User Guide.

A date of birth only has to be a valid date that is not in the
future, so a date such as 0001-01-01 is accepted. A typo such as
0950 for 1950 is saved without any warning.

No patient can be born before 1900, so such a date is almost certainly
an entry error.

Let's,
* reject dates of birth before 1900-01-01
* say the allowed range in the error message and the User Guide
* test the dates around the earliest allowed date

commitResults.messageTitle: Require phone numbers to start with 3, 6, 8 or 9
commitResults.messageBody:
A phone number only has to be 8 digits, so numbers such as 00000000
are accepted. Singapore phone numbers start with 3, 6, 8 or 9, so a
number starting with any other digit is almost certainly a typo.

Let's,
* require the first digit to be 3, 6, 8 or 9
* say so in the error message and the User Guide
* update test phone numbers that start with other digits

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject names with symbols not next to letters
commitResults.messageBody:
A name only has to start with a letter, so any mix of apostrophes,
hyphens, slashes and periods may follow it. Names such as
"Ben -- // .." are accepted, even though the symbols are not part of
any word.

In real names, these symbols join two letters, as in O'Brien,
Mary-Jane and s/o, or end a word, as in Jr.

Let's,
* only allow an apostrophe, hyphen or slash between two letters
* only allow a period right after a letter
* explain the rule in the error message and the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat curly apostrophes in names as straight ones
commitResults.messageBody:
Names typed with a curly apostrophe, such as O’Brien, are rejected.
Phones and word processors often replace ' with ’ automatically, so a
user who copies a name from a document may hit this error.

Accepting ’ as a separate character would let the same name be saved
in two ways, and find O'Brien would not find O’Brien.

Let's replace curly apostrophes with straight ones when parsing a
name, and mention this in the User Guide.

Patients cannot have appointments yet, but caregivers need to track
visits to each of a patient's providers.

The appointment commands need one class that holds an appointment's
details and checks that they are valid.

The checks are static methods, as in Name and Dob, so that both the
parser and storage can use them before creating an Appointment.

Let's,
* add an Appointment with a date, time, provider and optional note
* check dates, times and providers, with messages naming the field
* order appointments by date, then time

Commands such as addappt will need to read YYYY-MM-DD dates typed by
the user, but ParserUtil can only parse a date of birth, which must
not be in the future.

Let's,
* add ParserUtil.parseDate, which trims the input and rejects dates
  that do not exist, such as 2026-02-30

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep a sorted appointment list on each patient
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointments exist as a class, but a Patient cannot hold any.

Each patient needs their own list, kept in date and time order, so
that the appointment commands can refer to an appointment by its
number. addcare rebuilds the patient, so it must keep that list.

Sorting in the constructor keeps the order however a patient is
created. Saving and showing appointments come in the next two
commits, so loaded and sample patients start with none until then.

Let's,
* add a sorted list of appointments to Patient
* keep a patient's appointments when addcare adds care information
* start loaded and sample patients with no appointments for now

Appointments are only kept in memory, so they are lost when
MediConnect closes.

Data files saved before this change have no appointments and must
still load.

Let's,
* store each patient's appointments in the data file
* load a missing appointments list as an empty list
* reject an invalid or null appointment with a clear message

commitResults.messageTitle: Show appointments in the patient detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointments are saved with each patient, but the detail panel does
not show them, so a caregiver cannot see them.

Let's,
* add an Appointments section after Care Instructions, which shows
  "None recorded" when empty
* give two sample patients appointments, so new users see the section
* mention appointments in the User Guide's view section

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept only 4-digit years in appointment dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointment dates go through LocalDate.parse, which also accepts years
with a sign, such as +10000-01-01 or -0001-01-01. These are not in the
YYYY-MM-DD format that the error message and User Guide ask for.

Let's,
* check the date against a YYYY-MM-DD pattern before parsing it, as
  appointment times already do

Patient sorts its appointments by copying them into an ArrayList,
sorting it and copying it again. JsonAdaptedPatient and
PatientDetailPanel collect streams with Collectors.toList.
Stream#toList does each in one step and gives an unmodifiable list.
Stream#sorted keeps appointments at the same date and time in their
order, as Collections.sort did.

Let's,
* sort the appointments with stream().sorted().toList()
* use toList() in JsonAdaptedPatient and PatientDetailPanel

# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md

Patient sorts its appointments with stream().sorted().toList(), which
keeps a lone null entry, while every other list on Patient rejects
nulls through List.copyOf.

Let's,
* copy the appointments with List.copyOf before sorting them
* test that a null appointment is rejected

An Appointment can hold a time with seconds, such as 14:00:30. It
would be saved as 14:00:30, and loading it again fails, since
appointment times must be HH:MM.

Let's,
* reject a time with seconds in the Appointment constructor

commitResults.messageTitle: List upcoming appointments first in the panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel lists a patient's appointments by date and time, so
past ones come first. The plan asks for upcoming appointments first,
numbered, with commands using those numbers.

Let's,
* add Patient#getAppointmentsUpcomingFirst, which puts appointments at
  or after the given time first, then past ones, each by date and time
* use it in the detail panel, with the current time
* mention the order in the User Guide's view section

A few lines added for appointments in Patient, Appointment and
PatientBuilder are slightly over the 110-character soft limit.

Let's,
* wrap them

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore seconds when checking for past appointments
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointment#isBefore compares the appointment with the given time,
seconds included. At 12:00:30, an appointment at 12:00 counts as past,
although appointments are in whole minutes.

Let's,
* round the given time down to the minute in isBefore
* test an appointment in the current minute at 12:00:30
